transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, the main reason I came in is that I just get pulled off track so easily. It doesn't take much—like, one Slack ping, a random song lyric, or just an idea for another project popping into my head. And then suddenly I realize I've completely lost the thread of the dashboard I was supposed to be finishing. I just wanted to see if I could get some help with that.
Would you say this kind of distractibility has been a lifelong pattern for you, going back to childhood or school years, or is this something that started more recently?

Yeah, it's definitely been a lifelong pattern. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would always write comments about me... well, rushing through my worksheets and losing track of directions. They also mentioned I had a habit of talking over my classmates during group work. 

And at home, my parents actually used to sit right beside me while I did my homework. If they didn't, I would just wander off or start doing something else completely before I even finished what I was supposed to be working on. So, yeah, it's been going on for a long time.
Aside from the distractibility, do you often feel physically restless or fidgety, or have trouble staying seated for long periods, especially in situations like meetings or long car rides?

Yeah, I do. Especially when I have to sit through long classes or, like, portfolio reviews for my major. I'm almost always bouncing my leg or clicking my pen. Or I'll just be twisting my rings and shifting around in my chair a lot. I honestly don't really notice I'm doing it until someone looks over at me, but yeah, I definitely have a hard time just sitting completely still.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, blurting out answers before someone finishes a question, or having trouble waiting your turn in line or in discussions?

Yeah, I definitely do that. Um, especially when we're brainstorming for a project. I'll just kind of blurt out my idea right in the middle of someone talking. Or, like, if we're collaborating, I'll just start adding things to their Figma board before they've even finished explaining their thought. I just get really excited, but... I can usually tell afterward that I probably came off as pushy, even though I didn't mean to be.
